source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

import subprocess, pathlib, shutil, os, json
ZK="/workspace/executable"
def run(a,cwd="/tmp/nbp"):
    return subprocess.run([ZK]+a,cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True)
shutil.rmtree("/tmp/nbp",ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs("/tmp/nbp")
run(["--no-input","init"])
cases={
 "t01.md": "# Title With *Emphasis* and `Code` [Link](x.md)\n\nBody.\n",
 "t02.md": "Some intro paragraph.\n\n# Later Heading\n\nBody.\n",
 "t03.md": "#NoSpace Heading\n\nBody.\n",
 "t04.md": "# Title   \n\nBody trailing spaces   \n\n\n",
 "t05.md": "---\ntitle: FM Title\ntags: [TagOne, tag-two, 123]\ncount: 42\npi: 3.14\nok: true\nwhen: 2020-01-02\ndesc: \"Some: colon\"\nlist:\n  - a\n  - 2\n---\n# Heading\n\nBody #HashTag #tag-two #TAGONE end.\n",
 "t06.md": "# T6\n\n#tag at start, a#b, x #tag, (#paren), #tag. #tag, #tag: #tag; #under_score #-dash #\"quote\"\n",
 "t07.md": "# T7\n\n`#code-tag` [[#code]] \n\n```\n#codeblock-tag\n```\n\nReal #real-tag\n",
 "t08.md": "# T8\n\n:colon:tag: :a:b:c: x:y: :not closed and ::double::\n",
 "t09.md": "# T9\n\nMulti #word tag# and #multi word tag# end #single\n",
 "t10.md": "---\ntags:\n- one\n- two two\n---\nBody no heading #three\n",
 "t11.md": "---\nTitle: Capital Key\nTAGS: Upper\n---\nBody.\n",
 "t12.md": "---\ndate: \"2021-12-31\"\n---\n# T12\n\nBody.\n",
 "t13.md": "---\ndate: not-a-date\n---\n# T13\n\nBody.\n",
 "t14.md": "---\ndate: 2021-13-01\n---\n# T14\n\nBody.\n",
 "t15.md": "---invalid yaml: [\n---\n# T15\n\nBody #tag15\n",
 "t16.md": "# T16\n\n- List item one\n- Item two\n\n> Quote block line\n> second\n\nPara after.\n",
 "t17.md": "Title Setext\n============\n\nBody setext.\n",
 "t18.md": "## Sub Only\n\nBody.\n",
 "t19.md": "---\n---\n# T19\n\nBody.\n",
 "t20.md": "----\n# Not frontmatter\n\nBody.\n",
}
for k,v in cases.items(): pathlib.Path("/tmp/nbp",k).write_text(v)
run(["--no-input","index","--force"])
r=run(["--no-input","list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","json","--sort","path+"])
data=json.loads(r.stdout)
for n in data:
    print(n["path"], "| title=",repr(n["title"]), "| lead=",repr(n["lead"]), "| body=",repr(n["body"]), "| tags=",n["tags"], "| meta=",n["metadata"], "| created=",n["created"], "| wc=",n["wordCount"], "| snippets=",n["snippets"])
PY
cat /tmp/parse.txt"}

# ---------- Indexing ----------
def _walk_notebook_files(nb):
    # yields (abs_path, rel_path, is_dir?) files in Go filepath.Walk order (lexical per dir)
    root=nb.root
    results=[]
    def walk(dir_abs, rel_prefix):
        try:
            entries=list(os.scandir(dir_abs))
        except Exception:
            return
        entries.sort(key=lambda e: e.name)
        for entry in entries:
            name=entry.name
            if name.startswith('.'):
                continue
            rel = f"{rel_prefix}/{name}" if rel_prefix else name
            abs_path=os.path.join(dir_abs,name)
            try:
                is_dir=entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
                is_link=entry.is_symlink()
            except Exception:
                is_dir=False; is_link=False
            if is_dir and not is_link:
                walk(abs_path, rel)
            else:
                # file or symlink (to file or dir) treated as file entry
                results.append((abs_path, rel))
    walk(root,"")
    return results

def _match_glob(rel_path, pattern):
    # exclude globs: pattern matched against rel_path using path.Match-ish: * does not cross / ? "drafts/*" matches drafts/d1.md but not drafts/sub?
    # Implement fnmatch but * should not cross '/' for single segment patterns? Original Go path.Match: * matches non-separator sequence.
    # Convert glob to regex
    def glob_to_regex(pat):
        out="^"; i=0
        while i<len(pat):
            ch=pat[i]
            if ch=='*':
                if i+1<len(pat) and pat[i+1]=='*':
                    out+='.*'; i+=2; continue
                out+='[^/]*'; i+=1; continue
            elif ch=='?': out+='[^/]'; i+=1; continue
            elif ch=='[':
                j=pat.find(']',i)
                if j==-1: out+='\\['; i+=1; continue
                out+=pat[i:j+1]; i=j+1; continue
            else: out+=re.escape(ch); i+=1
        out+='$'; return out
    return re.match(glob_to_regex(pattern), rel_path) is not None

def index_notebook(nb, force=False, verbose=False):
    con=nb.open_db()

                    out+='.*'; i+=2; continue
                out+='[^/]*'; i+=1; continue
            elif ch=='?': out+='[^/]'; i+=1; continue
            elif ch=='[':

                if j==-1: out+='\\['; i+=1; continue
                out+=pat[i:j+1]; i=j+1; continue
            else: out+=re.escape(ch); i+=1
        out+='$'; return out

See earlier probes: force on existing DB (notes existed) counted modified; fresh force counted added.
            status='modified' if existing_row else 'added'

                if db_mod_ns!=mtime_ns or existing_row['checksum']!=checksum:

            verbose_lines.append((rel,f"- unchanged {rel}"))

def _sort_metadata(obj):
    if isinstance(obj,dict):
        return {k:_sort_metadata(obj[k]) for k in sorted(obj.keys())}
    if isinstance(obj,list):
        return [_sort_metadata(x) for x in obj]
    return obj

def _stem_of_path(path):
    dirpart=os.path.dirname(path)
    base=os.path.basename(path)
    if '.' in base:
        stem=base.rsplit('.',1)[0]
    else: stem=base
    return f"{dirpart}/{stem}" if dirpart else stem

def _resolve_link(link, source_rel, source_dir, note_map, note_stem_map, nb):
    raw_href=link.href_raw.strip() if isinstance(link.href_raw,str) else link.href_raw
    is_external=link.is_external
    if link.type=='wiki-link':
        href=raw_href
        if is_external:
            return href, None, True
        if href.startswith('#'):
            # anchor only
            return href, note_map.get(source_rel), False
        # strip anchor for resolution
        target_ref=href.split('#',1)[0]
        if target_ref=='':
            return href, note_map.get(source_rel), False
        # match stem or full path
        if target_ref in note_map:
            return href, note_map[target_ref], False
        if target_ref in note_stem_map:
            return href, note_stem_map[target_ref], False
        # also maybe with extension stripped if href has .md
        return href, None, False
    else: # markdown
        href_raw=raw_href
        if is_external:
            return href_raw, None, True
        if href_raw.startswith('#'):

        # percent decode
        from urllib.parse import unquote
        href_decoded=unquote(href_raw)
        # strip fragment/query for resolution and stored? Original: what does it store for md link with anchor? Keep decoded href minus? We'll test approximate: store normalized path with fragment preserved? For now if '#' in decoded, split

        fragment=''
        if '#' in href_decoded:
            # Only if it's not start; keep ?
            parts=href_decoded.split('#',1)
            # If the path part contains .md or / etc, treat fragment separately
            # Go markdown parser link destination includes fragment; their resolution may strip it and stored href may be path only?
            href_path=parts[0]
            fragment='#'+parts[1] if parts[1] else ''
        else:
            href_path=href_decoded
        if href_path=='':
            return href_raw, note_map.get(source_rel), False
        # Normalize relative to source_dir using Go join
        if os.path.isabs(href_path):
            # Go filepath.Join(source_dir, "/a.md") = source_dir/a.md (relative treatment)
            normalized=go_join(source_dir, href_path)
        else:
            normalized=go_join(source_dir, href_path) if source_dir else os.path.normpath(href_path)
        href_stored=normalized+fragment if False else normalized  # fragment stripped for stored as per guess: test after
        # If href_stored is outside notebook (..), target none
        if href_stored=='..' or href_stored.startswith('../'):
            return href_stored, None, False
        if href_stored in note_map:
            return href_stored, note_map[href_stored], False
        if href_stored in note_stem_map:
            return href_stored, note_stem_map[href_stored], False
        # If no extension, maybe add?
        return href_stored, None, False

# clean INITFILE
pathlib.Path("/tmp/INITFILE").write_text("x") if False else None

    pathlib.Path(root,".hidden.md").write_text("# H\n\nx\n")
    pathlib.Path(root,"sub").mkdir(exist_ok=True); pathlib.Path(root,"sub/c.md").write_text("# C\n\nx\n")
cases=[C(["--no-input","index"]),C(["--no-input","index","--verbose"]),C(["--no-input","index","--force","--verbose"]),C(["--no-input","index","--quiet"]),C(["--no-input","index","-v","-f","-q"])]
do_compare("index",setup2,cases)

# alias via compare tree? Use direct
def alias_trial():
    for label,b in [("orig",ORIG),("mine",MINE)]:
        root=f"/tmp/dtalias_{label}"; shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root); run(b,["--no-input","init"],cwd=root)
        pathlib.Path(root,"a.md").write_text("# A\n\nBody\n")
        cfg=pathlib.Path(root,".zk/config.toml"); txt=cfg.read_text(); cfg.write_text(txt.replace("[alias]",'[alias]\nhello = "echo hello $@"\nls = "zk list $@"\nbad = "false"\nshowenv = "echo NB=$ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR"'))

import subprocess, os, pathlib, shutil
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; MINE="/tmp/my_zk"
def run(b,args,cwd,env=None):
    e=os.environ.copy()
    for k in ["ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR","ZK_EDITOR","VISUAL","EDITOR"]: e.pop(k,None)
    if env: e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run([b]+args,cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
tests=[]
# Use /tmp/nbg and /tmp/nb2 as existing notebooks from original (but indexing via mine will modify their DBs - copy them to separate dirs per binary)
for label,b in [("orig",ORIG),("mine",MINE)]:
    for src,dst in [("/tmp/nbg","/tmp/disc_"+label),("/tmp/nb2","/tmp/disc2_"+label)]:
        if os.path.exists(dst): shutil.rmtree(dst)
        shutil.copytree(src,dst, symlinks=True)
    root=f"/tmp/disc_{label}"
    outs=[]
    for args,cwd,env in [
        (["list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","{{path}}"],root,None),
        (["list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","{{path}}"],root+"/sub",None),
        (["--notebook-dir",root,"list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","{{path}}"],"/tmp",None),
        (["list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","{{path}}"],"/tmp",{"ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR":root}),
        (["--working-dir",root,"list","--no-pager","--quiet","--format","{{path}}"],"/tmp",None),
        (["--notebook-dir","/tmp/nonexist123","list"],"/tmp",None),
        (["list"],"/tmp",{"ZK_NOTEBOOK_DIR":"/tmp/nonexist123"}),
        (["--working-dir","/tmp/nonexist123","list"],"/tmp",None),
        (["list"],"/tmp",None),
        (["--notebook-dir",root+"/sub/e.md","list","--no-pager","--quiet"],"/tmp",None),
    ]:
        r=run(b,args,cwd=cwd,env=env); outs.append((args[0],r.returncode,r.stdout.replace(root,"/NB").replace("/tmp/disc_","/NBROOT_"),r.stderr.replace(root,"/NB")))
    globals()[label]=outs
    print(label, outs)
print("match?", globals()["orig"]==globals()["mine"])
for i,(o,m) in enumerate(zip(globals()["orig"],globals()["mine"])):
    if o!=m: print("diff",i,o,m)
PY
python3 /tmp/test_discovery.py 2>&1 | tail -n 100

def apply_style(style_str, text, env):
    if text=='':
        # style helper on empty still may validate
        pass
    rules=style_str.split() if style_str else []
    seqs=[]
    has_attr=False; has_color=False; has_bg=False
    for r in rules:
        if r in _STYLE_ATTRS:
            seqs.append(f"\x1b[{_STYLE_ATTRS[r]}m"); has_attr=True
        elif r in _STYLE_COLORS:
            seqs.append(f"\x1b[{_STYLE_COLORS[r]}m"); has_color=True
        elif r.endswith('-bg'):
            base=r[:-3]
            if base in _STYLE_COLORS:
                seqs.append(f"\x1b[{_STYLE_COLORS[base]+10}m"); has_bg=True
            else:
                env.warn(f"zk: warning: unknown styling rule: {r}")
        else:
            env.warn(f"zk: warning: unknown styling rule: {r}")
    if not env.style_enabled or not seqs:
        return text
    # termenv-like: prefix sequences combined? Our separate sequences are equivalent visually but raw for predefined formats need combined?
    # Predefined templates produce sequences as separate ESC[1m ESC[33m etc when captured via pane; raw pipe via pager had combined 1;33.
    # Termenv actually outputs \x1b[1;33m when writing directly? Captured pane converts.
    # We'll emit each sequence separately to match pane capture segments: \x1b[1m\x1b[33m text \x1b[0m\x1b[39m\x1b[49m
    prefix=''.join(seqs)
    # reset logic based on original: if any attribute, reset includes 0m 39m 49m; if only color, only 39m (fg) or 49m (bg)
    if has_attr:
        suffix="\x1b[0m\x1b[39m\x1b[49m"
    elif has_color and has_bg:
        suffix="\x1b[39m\x1b[49m"
    elif has_color:
        suffix="\x1b[39m"
    elif has_bg:
        suffix="\x1b[49m"
    else:
        suffix="\x1b[0m"
    return prefix+text+suffix

    para=[]  # list of (content, off, end)
    def flush_para():
        nonlocal para

            fc=fence_match.group(1)[0]; fl=len(fence_match.group(1))

                in_fence=True; fence_char=fc; fence_len=fl
            elif fc==fence_char and fl>=fence_len:
                in_fence=False
            flush_para(); continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        if stripped=='':
            flush_para(); continue
        # Setext underline: applies to current paragraph
        setext=re.match(r'^ {0,3}(=+|-+)[ \\t]*$', content)
        if setext and para:
            level=1 if setext.group(1).startswith('=') else 2
            title=''.join(_inline_plain(l[0].strip()) for l in para)
            candidates.append((level, para[0][1], title, para[0][2]))
            flush_para(); continue
        # ATX heading
        m=re.match(r'^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \\t]+(.*)$', content)
        if m:
            level=len(m.group(1))
            heading_text=m.group(2).strip()
            heading_text=re.sub(r'[ \\t]+#+[ \\t]*$', '', heading_text)
            title=_inline_plain(heading_text)

        if re.match(r'^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \\t]*$', content):
            level=len(re.match(r'^ {0,3}(#{1,6})[ \\t]*$', content).group(1))
            candidates.append((level, off, '', end)); flush_para(); continue
        # Block starts that interrupt paragraph for our purposes
        if re.match(r'^ {0,3}([-*+] |\\d+\\. | >|>)', content) or re.match(r'^ {0,3}([-*_])(\\s*\\1){2,}\\s*$', content):

            continue
        # Regular paragraph line

    if not candidates:

    candidates_sorted=sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1]))
    level, first_off, title, body_start = candidates_sorted[0]

def cmd_tag_list(parsed, nb):
    index_notebook(nb, force=False, verbose=False)
    notes=fetch_notes(nb)
    con=nb.open_db()
    tags=[]
    # count tags by collection id order for counts? Tag list query: count per collection where notes exist
    for row in con.execute("SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(nc.note_id) FROM collections c JOIN notes_collections nc ON nc.collection_id=c.id WHERE c.kind='tag' GROUP BY c.id, c.name"):
        tags.append({'id':row[0],'kind':'tag','name':row[1],'noteCount':row[2]})
    # sort validation for tags
    try:
        terms=parse_sort_terms(parsed.flags.get('sort',[]), kind='tag')
    except AppError:
        raise
    tags_sorted=sort_tags(tags, terms)
    # rendering
    fmt=parsed.flags.get('format','') or ''
    header=decode_sep(parsed.flags.get('header',''))
    footer=decode_sep(parsed.flags.get('footer',"\\n"))
    delimiter=decode_sep(parsed.flags.get('delimiter',"\\n"))
    delim0=parsed.flags.get('delimiter0',False)
    items=[]
    env=make_render_env(nb)
    if fmt=='json':
        items=['['+','.join(go_json_dumps_tag(t) for t in tags_sorted)+']']
    elif fmt=='jsonl':
        items=[go_json_dumps_tag(t) for t in tags_sorted]
    elif fmt in ('name','full',''):
        use='full' if fmt in ('full','') else 'name'
        for t in tags_sorted:
            if use=='name':
                # style? tag name in tty maybe no style
                items.append(t['name'])
            else:
                items.append(f"{t['name']} ({t['noteCount']})")
    else:
        try:
            from template_engine import parse_template
            parse_template(fmt)
        except TemplateParseError as e:
            raise AppError(f"load template failed: {e}")
        for t in tags_sorted:
            ctx={'kind':t['kind'],'name':t['name'],'noteCount':t['noteCount'],'note-count':t['noteCount'],'__hidden_id':t['id']}
            try:
                items.append(render_template(fmt, ctx, env))
            except TemplateEvalError as e:
                msg=e.args[0] if e.args else str(e); node=getattr(e,'current_node',None)
                if node: msg+=f"\nCurrent node:\n\t{node}"
                raise AppError(f"render template failed: Evaluation error: {msg}")
            except TemplateFatal as e:
                raise FatalMessage(str(e))
    if not items:
        text=""
    elif delim0:
        text="".join(item+"\x00" for item in items)
    else:
        # json empty case items = ['[]'] should still print
        text=header+delimiter.join(items)+footer
    if tags_sorted or fmt=='json':
        # If tags empty but json format, items ['[]'] text already
        pass
    else:
        if not tags_sorted:
            text=""
    output_with_pager(nb, text, no_pager=parsed.flags.get('no-pager',False))
    if not parsed.flags.get('quiet',False):
        sys.stderr.write(f"\nFound {len(tags_sorted)} {plural('tag',len(tags_sorted))}\n")
    return 0

def _strip_comment(line, in_str=False):
    # We'll parse char by char in main parser instead
    pass

class Parser:
    def __init__(self, text):
        if text.startswith('\ufeff'): text=text[1:]
        self.text=text
        self.lines=text.splitlines()
        self.data={}
        self.positions={}
        self.current_path=[]  # list of keys
        self.current_dict=self.data
        self.defined_tables=set()
        self.defined_keys=set()
        # root defined
    def parse(self):
        i=0
        while i < len(self.lines):
            raw=self.lines[i]
            lineno=i+1
            stripped=self._strip_comment_outside(raw).strip()
            if not stripped:
                i+=1; continue
            if stripped.startswith('['):
                # table header, could be [[array]] - not in config, treat error/unsupported
                if stripped.startswith('[['):
                    raise TomlError("was expecting token =, but got \"[[\" instead", lineno, 1)
                # find closing ]
                end=self._find_closing_bracket(raw)
                if end==-1:
                    # try tokenize error similar: was expecting token ...
                    raise TomlError("was expecting token =, but got \""+stripped[1:].strip()+"\" instead", lineno, 9 if len(raw)>=9 else 1)
                header=stripped[1:end].strip()
                rest=stripped[end+1:].strip()
                if rest:
                    raise TomlError(f"was expecting token =, but got \"{rest}\" instead", lineno, end+2)
                path=self._parse_key_path(header, lineno)
                # duplicate table check
                dotted='.'.join(path)
                if dotted in self.defined_tables:
                    raise TomlError("duplicated tables", lineno, 2)
                self.defined_tables.add(dotted)
                # navigate/create
                d=self.data
                for k in path:
                    if k not in d:
                        d[k]={}
                    elif not isinstance(d[k], dict):
                        raise TomlError("duplicated tables", lineno, 2)
                    d=d[k]
                self.current_path=path
                self.current_dict=d
                i+=1; continue
            else:
                # key = value (value may span multiple lines if array or string multiline)
                # Find = outside strings
                eq=self._find_eq(raw)
                if eq==-1:
                    # error: was expecting token =, but got "X" instead. Determine second token
                    tokens=stripped.split()
                    bad=tokens[1] if len(tokens)>1 else (tokens[0] if tokens else "")
                    if bad.startswith('[['): bad='[['
                    # column of bad token in raw (1-indexed) approx
                    col=raw.find(bad)+1 if bad in raw else 1
                    raise TomlError(f"was expecting token =, but got \"{bad}\" instead", lineno, col)
                key_raw=raw[:eq].strip()
                if not key_raw:
                    raise TomlError("was expecting token =, but got \"=\" instead", lineno, eq+1)
                key_path=self._parse_key_path(key_raw, lineno)
                full_path=self.current_path+key_path
                dotted='.'.join(full_path)
                if dotted in self.defined_keys or dotted in self.defined_tables:
                    raise TomlError(f"The following key was defined twice: {dotted}", lineno, 1)
                value_text=raw[eq+1:]
                # If value empty -> expecting a value error at next line (as observed (next line,1))
                if not self._strip_comment_outside(value_text).strip():
                    raise TomlError("expecting a value", lineno+1, 1)
                # Join continuation lines for multiline arrays / multiline strings
                value_str=value_text
                start_line=lineno
                # collect until balanced or multiline string closed
                while not self._value_complete(value_str):
                    i+=1
                    if i>=len(self.lines):
                        break
                    value_str+="\n"+self.lines[i]
                # parse value
                val=self._parse_value(value_str, start_line, eq+2)
                # store
                d=self.current_dict
                for k in key_path[:-1]:
                    if k not in d: d[k]={}
                    d=d[k]
                leaf=key_path[-1]
                if leaf in d:
                    raise TomlError(f"The following key was defined twice: {dotted}", lineno, 1)
                d[leaf]=val
                self.defined_keys.add(dotted)
                self.positions[dotted]=(start_line,1,val)
                i+=1; continue
        return ParsedToml(self.data, self.positions)
    def _find_closing_bracket(self, raw):
        in_basic=False; in_literal=False; esc=False
        for idx,ch in enumerate(raw):
            if in_basic:
                if esc: esc=False
                elif ch=='\\': esc=True
                elif ch=='"': in_basic=False
                continue
            if in_literal:
                if ch=="'": in_literal=False
                continue
            if ch=='"': in_basic=True
            elif ch=="'": in_literal=True
            elif ch==']': return idx
            elif ch=='#': break
        return -1

def _mask_links(masked):
    chars=list(masked)
    # wiki
    for m in re.finditer(r'\[\[[^\]]*\]\]', masked):
        for k in range(m.start(), m.end()): chars[k]=' ' if chars[k] not in '\r\n' else chars[k]
    s=''.join(chars)
    # markdown links: replace entire [text](dest) or [text][ref]
    def repl(m):
        return ''.join(' ' if c not in '\r\n' else c for c in m.group(0))
    # Preserve link text (tags can appear there) but mask destinations
    def repl_dest(m):
        # group1 is [text], rest is destination part to mask
        txt=m.group(1)
        rest=m.group(0)[len(txt):]
        return txt+''.join(' ' if c not in '\r\n' else c for c in rest)
    s=re.sub(r'(!?\[[^\]]*\])(\([^)]*\))', repl_dest, s)
    s=re.sub(r'(!?\[[^\]]*\])(\[[^\]]*\])', repl_dest, s)
    return s
